newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE WANT STARS FOR NEXT SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE WANT STARS FOR NEXT SEASON.

text.p: Former European soccer champions Marseille plan to sign a lot of promising youngsters and a couple of stars in their bid to make it back to the top of French soccer next season.

"We need a couple of big stars because the Marseille crowd likes them and because we need them to reach a European cup competition which will be our main goal next season," Marseille boss Robert Louis-Dreyfus told sports daily l'Equipe on Monday.
Louis-Dreyfus, who is also Adidas chairman, said Denmark's Michael Laudrup might be one of the new signings. The 32-year-old Laudrup plays in Japan's J League for Vissel Kobe.

Marseille would have liked to sign up Italians Roberto Baggio or Gianfranco Zola but Louis-Dreyfus said Baggio was under contract with a rival sportswear company and he wanted only players linked with Adidas.
As for Zola, who won the F.A. Cup with Chelsea on Saturday: "The English would not let him go," he said.
Marseille confirmed on Saturday that former Bordeaux coach Rolland Courbis would be the team's manager next season.
Courbis said his goal would be to finish in the league's top five. "I'm back in my home town. I think we must start all over again," said Courbis.

In order to build a new team, Louis-Dreyfus said he wanted to employ promising players on a long-term basis. "Our main concern is to sign five-year contracts with young skilled players aged between 21 and 25," he said.

Among players almost certain to play in Marseille next season are Yugoslav striker Anto Drobnjak and French internationals Claude Makelele and Christophe Dugarry as well as reserve goalkeeper Francois Lemasson.
Bulgaria's Iordan Lechkov and Italian defenders Ivan Franceschini and Alberto Malusci are leaving.
